subject: Post-call: Deployment options & noisy-neighbor concerns (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: Deployment options & noisy-neighbor concerns (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks again for taking the time today, Nora — good conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on deployment mode and the isolation concerns you raised.

Recap from our call:
- FinPay primary constraints: PCI-scope workloads, strict p95 latency target, and a requirement for predictable tail latency during peak payroll batch windows.
- Deployment options discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity (isolated GPU pools), Private VPC / on-prem (full network isolation).
- Key concern: noisy-neighbor effects on shared infrastructure leading to tail-latency spikes and potential SLA exposure. You asked for: (1) typical noisy-neighbor mitigations, (2) isolation boundaries for Dedicated, and (3) how we measure SLOs and alerting.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf (high-level SLA & capacity lead times), network-isolation-diagram.png (logical isolation boundaries).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (30-45m) to review telemetry and actual isolation mechanics — can we do Wed or Thu next week?
2) If you'd like, we can scope a short performance spike test (canary) on a Dedicated pool to surface any tail behavior before commit.
3) Please share your target p95, qps during peak, and any SOC2 or procurement documents (I saw you have a questionnaire) — I attached a sample response matrix.

Questions for you (quick):
- Target p95 latency requirement? (ms)
- Peak concurrent requests / sustained qps during payroll windows?
- Any non-negotiable networking constraints (no egress to third-party regions, etc.)?

Happy to jump on a short call to run through answers.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment options & noisy-neighbor concerns (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks, Priyom — helpful recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side:

- p95 target: 150 ms (application-level, end-to-end for inference).
- Peak: ~250 requests/sec sustained for a 20-30 minute payroll window; bursts up to ~400 rps for short periods.
- PCI requirement: We need either Dedicated capacity with strict tenancy or Private VPC/on-prem. Shared Hosted is acceptable only for non-PCI workloads.

Security has attached our SOC2 questions matrix — point them at the security team if needed. We also need visibility into per-tenant telemetry (latency histograms, per-instance CPU/GPU utilization) for our compliance logs.

I think a Dedicated reserved pool with a canary run sounds good — are you able to show how you guarantee isolation (scheduling, hypervisor/container boundaries, kernel flags) and how that maps to SLOs?

We'd like a TTD for technical deep-dive: Tue 4/20 16:00 or Wed 4/21 10:00 ET.

Best,
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | FinPay
nora.patel@finpay.com

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment options & noisy-neighbor concerns (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks for the details, Nora — that helps a lot. Confirming next steps and a few clarifications below.

Answers / proposed approach:
- Given 150 ms p95 and sustained 250 rps with bursts to 400 rps for PCI workloads, our recommendation is Dedicated reserved capacity (isolated GPU pools) with a short canary in your environment. Dedicated gives predictable scheduling and network isolation; we can also offer a Private VPC if you require customer-managed networking or on-prem.
- Isolation guarantees: for Dedicated we use tenant-pinned GPU pools (no co-scheduling of unrelated tenants), per-tenant cgroup and NUMA pinning, and kernel-level mitigations for noisy-disk/IO. The network diagram attached shows the isolation boundaries and where KMS / audit logs sit. We'll bring our infra engineer to the deep-dive to walk through specifics (scheduling, eviction policies, preemption controls, and telemetry hooks).
- Telemetry: we expose per-tenant latency histograms, per-instance GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, and tail-latency alerts. We can ship a daily SLO report and a realtime trace link for any incident.

Scheduling: Tue 20 Apr 2027 16:00 ET works for our infra lead — I've tentatively booked a 45m slot. Would you like to include Security on that call?

Attachments: finpay-soc2-questions.xlsx (as requested).

Next items for us to prepare before the call:
- Short canary test plan (10-15m run with load profile) + expected metrics to validate isolation.
- SLA & lead-time doc for Dedicated deployments (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf).
- Link to HubSpot deal for procurement cadence: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/FP-2024-087

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the deep-dive agenda.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
